data.expected: Design ruling for the open MEMORY_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN section 4.2 choice: use one canonical ByteStore per nominal backing-storage identity, not write propagation over an alias graph. An allocation record is a live typed view naming a backing StorageId, a nonnegative backing origin, its local extent, address space/source/placement, permissions, epoch, and ownership. Reads and writes translate the allocation-local range into one checked backing-store span; two views alias exactly where their translated spans overlap. Relative signed shifts are derived from view origins rather than installed independently. Allocation creates a fresh backing identity and its initial view; mapping creates another view only through a checked provider/API transition that proves the backing relationship and exact range, carries its mapping/unmapping obligations, and preserves the memory-state invariant. Unmapping invalidates that view/provenance without destroying backing bytes still held by another live view; backing teardown has its own last-owner/obligation rule. Keep raw backing/view constructors private or explicitly test-only. Derive SharesBytes, range overlap, conflicts, and grant coverage from backing identity plus translated spans; do not retain a second mutable alias graph as an authority source. This makes byte coherence definitional and localizes framing to canonical backing spans instead of re-proving write propagation through every alias path. Add negative fixtures for fabricated unrelated mappings, inconsistent/out-of-bounds view origins, stale/unmapped views, and destroying backing storage with live views; add positive nonzero-offset mapped-view read-after-write in both directions and unmapping-preserves-other-view fixtures. The current authority-only alias API may remain only as clearly provisional non-consumable scaffolding until this replacement lands; no MemoryProfile or VerifiedProgram-facing transition may depend on it.

It does not challenge collision in the source/profile digest functions themselves. Two different actual sources with the same source Digest are definitionally the same SemanticEnvironment; the type has nowhere to retain their difference, so replay? accepts and Eq.rec transports the cached certificate. Design ruling: manifestRoot is a canonical, domain-separated manifest digest, not the cache key or artifact digest. Every manifest node exposes both manifestRoot and publicSummary uniformly. A leaf root is computed from a leaf tag, scope, the exact semantic-environment preimage retained by CacheRecord, publicSummary, and artifact digest; build measurement and disposition are excluded because they are observations of a build, not semantic identity. An aggregate root is computed from an aggregate tag, scope, its ordered direct ChildSummary vector, and aggregate publicSummary; measurement is excluded. Prefer computed projections, or a stored digest paired with a rootExact equality, over caller-supplied unconstrained fields. Add publicSummary to AggregateManifest. ChildSummary values at an aggregate must be derived from the actual child nodes/certificates with an exact vector alignment proof (for example children = childNodes.map ManifestNode.toChildSummary), not accepted as unrelated digest triples. Hash equality remains lookup/bookkeeping only and never establishes Lean soundness; the imported child certificate and structural alignment carry proof authority. This closes the forged-child-summary seam in g-design:215 rather than merely choosing a hash name.

data.summary: Three-part implementation ruling for Decision 134. (1) Break the cycle with a nonrecursive exported ProcessContractView declared before ProcessRequirement and SpecProcess. ProcessRequirement.acceptable ranges only over that view plus an exact match to its RequiredProcessContract; after SpecProcess exists, SelectedProcessRequirementWitness may carry a SpecProcess and its projection equality. A requirement can never inspect a witness's private state or topology. (2) The suite explicitly supplies the finite capability selection it uses. ResourceModel need not enumerate every possible axis. Exactness means the snapshot is complete for that selected suite capability set, not for all ambient instances on R; rename ExactSnapshotOfEntireCapabilityMap if necessary to make that boundary unambiguous. Downstream code never repeats instance search. (3) Add a finite keyed theorem family to SpecificationSuite. Each TheoremDemand must be extensional under the project's exact behavior-equivalence relation, either by construction or by an explicit preservation proof. Define MeetsAllSpecificationTheorems spec as the dependent forall over every key at spec's captured context. PortableProgramCertificate must carry both exact behavioral equivalence to spec.contract and that keyed dependent family; its legacy terminal accepts theorem is only a derived projection. VerifiedProgram exposes each keyed proof for the loaded artifact by composing exact equivalence through driver, provider, machine, and artifact refinements. Empty families, reflexive aliases, or a monolithic replacement field are invalid.
verification: The exported-view split removes the negative declaration cycle while retaining existential SpecProcess witnesses after the root is declared.
Finite explicit selection implements the already-ratified construction-time snapshot without imposing a closed global resource-axis inventory.
Equivalence-respecting keyed demands let spec-level correctness remain precious while exact artifact equivalence transports every demanded property independently.
